newsitem.title: USA: Moody's, S&P eye negative review for AMR munis.
newsitem.headline: Moody's, S&P eye negative review for AMR munis.

text.p: The ratings on AMR Corp's special facility municipal revenue debt, issued for airport projects, may be reviewed for possible downgrade if pilots strike AMR's American Airlines, according to analysts from Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp.
Renee Shaker, a vice president and senior analyst at Moody's, said the rating agency's actions would depend on the "facts and circumstances" of any strike.
Still, she said the rating on the debt could go on review for possible downgrade if a strike figured to be protracted and costly.
Phil Baggaley, a managing director at S&P, said that "if and when the strike starts," AMR's rating may be placed on negative CreditWatch.
He said a strike could be long and expensive for the airline, or the carrier could end up with a costly agreement with the pilots' union.
Baggaley said AMR's BB-plus rating had been given a positive outlook last year.
Industry analysts say a strike could cost the airline $30 million a day.
The pilots have threatened to walk out at midnight Friday.
